tips.intro: Books Tower is a one-button stacking game. A book slides back and forth above a wooden table, you drop it onto the pile, and each book that stays on adds one point. These tips come from several short runs in the browser.
tips: Drop when the moving book is right above the top of the pile. The book falls straight down from wherever it is at the moment you press, so the timing decides where it lands.
Watch the book, not the score. The score sits at the top center and only changes after a book has landed, so it is no help for timing the next drop.
Small misses are fine. In testing, books that landed a little to the left or right of the one below still stayed on the pile, and every book kept its full size.
A clearly mistimed drop ends the run. The results screen then appears at once, so treat every drop as the one that counts.
Use a short, firm press rather than a very fast click. In testing a few very quick clicks did not drop the book, while a short press of the mouse button worked every time.
After a few off-center books the pile starts to lean, so aim the next drop back toward the middle of the table instead of following the lean.
tips.conclusion: Press when the sliding book is over the top of the pile, use a firm click, and steer the tower back toward the middle when it starts to drift. One clear miss ends the run.

extra_sections.heading: What one run looked like
paragraphs: A run starts with a single book lying on the table and a score of 0. The next book, in a different color, slides left and right near the top of the screen. Three books dropped near the center gave a score of 3, with a purple, an orange and a blue book stacked slightly out of line.
When a drop went wrong, the game switched straight to the results screen with the final score in large numbers.

controls.intro: Books Tower needs only one action. Every drop is a single press of the left mouse button, and the menus use the same button.
controls.desktop: Press the left mouse button anywhere on the game to drop the sliding book. A short, firm press worked best in testing. The round play button starts a run, and the other round buttons on the title and results screens are clicked the same way. No keyboard keys were needed.
tips: The large blue play button starts a new run from the title screen or the results screen.
The orange speaker button at the top of the title screen is the sound control.
The orange share button and the pink trophy button sit on either side of the play button.
The pink house button at the top of the results screen goes back to the title screen.

beginner-guide.intro: New to Books Tower? Here is how to get from the loading screen to your first run, and what the screens show.
beginner-guide.what_it_is: Books Tower, shown on its title screen as Books Tower Challenge, is a free browser stacking game. A single book lies on a wooden table. Another book slides back and forth near the top of the screen, and you press to drop it onto the pile. Each book that lands adds one point to the score at the top. A drop that misses ends the run and shows your score. There are no levels or menus to learn, so a run starts within seconds.
first_steps: Click OK, PLAY NOW! on the loading screen.
On the Books Tower Challenge title screen, press the large blue play button.
Watch the sliding book for a couple of passes to get a feel for its speed.
Press when it is directly above the book on the table. The score goes up by one when it lands.
Keep each new book close to the middle of the pile so the tower does not drift too far to one side.
When the run ends, press the blue play button on the results screen to try again.
beginner-guide.who_its_for: Players who want a quick timing game they can pick up for a minute. It uses one button, and each run is short.

extra_sections.heading: The results screen
paragraphs: At the end of a run the screen shows Players Online, your score in large numbers, a BEST line and a Your Rank line. Under that are the share, play and trophy buttons, and a REVIVE? option with a film icon. The revive option was not tried during testing.

similar.intro: Books Tower is all about one well-timed press. A piece slides back and forth, you drop it, and the tower grows one book at a time until a single bad drop ends the run. If you like that kind of short timing challenge, look for other stacking and one-click games where each run takes a minute or two, the score is simply how far you got, and trying again is one click away. Games where pieces drop straight down from a moving starting point feel closest. On Pixelsprout, Tower Blocks Deluxe 3D, Stack Block - Up, Color Tower 2 - Drop The Boxes 3D and BuildTower are built around the same idea of stacking pieces into a tower.
similar.title: Stacking Games Online Free: Games Like Books Tower
similar.meta_description: What makes a stacking game, plus six free stacking and drop games you can play in the browser on Pixelsprout, starting with Books Tower.

extra_sections.heading: What makes a stacking game
paragraphs: A stacking game gives you one piece at a time and asks you to place it on top of the last one. Usually the piece moves on its own, sliding side to side or swinging, and you press once to drop it. The score is how many pieces stay on the pile, and a run ends when a piece misses or the tower falls.

Most stacking games are about timing rather than planning. You watch the moving piece, wait for it to line up with the top of the pile, and drop. Some games trim the part that hangs over the edge, so a bad drop makes the next one harder. Others keep every piece whole and let the tower lean instead.

extra_sections.heading: Books Tower in short
paragraphs: In Books Tower a book slides back and forth above a wooden table, and one press of the left mouse button drops it. Each book that lands adds one point. In our play, books that landed a little off center stayed on the pile at full size and made the tower lean, and one clearly mistimed drop ended the run at once.

extra_sections.heading: Stacking games to try next
paragraphs: Tower Blocks Deluxe 3D: going by its game description, you drop blocks one by one to build a skyscraper in 3D, and the challenge gets harder with every level. A bad drop can bring the tower down.
Stack Block - Up: its description is about building a tall tower block by block, where timing decides each placement and the goal is a high score.
Color Tower 2 - Drop The Boxes 3D: according to its description, you build a tower from colored boxes in 3D, using quick reflexes, with global leaderboards for height.
BuildTower: its description says the game has several levels, each with a different target height, and each floor shows a best spot to place the next piece.

extra_sections.heading: Two more drop and stack games
paragraphs: MetaStack: its description calls it a one-player stacking challenge where you build a tower block by block, aim for the perfect drop, and use power-ups along the way.

Color Tower: going by its description, you drop colored boxes to build a skyscraper, levels get harder as you go, and missed drops make your boxes smaller. That is the main difference from Books Tower, where books kept their size in our play.

faqs.question: How do you play Books Tower?
faqs.answer: A book slides back and forth above the pile. Press the left mouse button to drop it. If it lands on the pile you get one point, and the next book starts sliding.

faqs.question: What ends a run in Books Tower?
faqs.answer: A badly timed drop. In testing, the game went straight to the results screen after a drop that went wrong, showing the final score.

faqs.question: Does the book get smaller if it lands off center?
faqs.answer: Not in testing. Books that landed a little to one side stayed on the pile at their full size, which made the tower lean slightly.

faqs.question: Why did my click not drop the book?
faqs.answer: In testing, a few very quick clicks did not register as a drop. A short, firm press of the mouse button dropped the book every time.

faqs.question: Are there levels in Books Tower?
faqs.answer: None were seen. Each run starts from one book on the table and a score of 0, and you keep stacking until a drop misses.

faqs.question: What is the REVIVE option?
faqs.answer: The results screen shows REVIVE? with a film icon under the play button. It was not pressed during testing, so what it does was not checked.

faqs.question: Do I need the keyboard?
faqs.answer: No. Every drop and every button on the title and results screens works with the left mouse button.
